title: Impact of Road Density on Urban Population Growth

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use **Instrumental Variables (IV)** estimation with the 1947 highway plan as an instrument for road density. This leverages historical transportation planning decisions that were likely made based on factors orthogonal to contemporary population growth determinants. The key assumptions are: (1) **Relevance**: The 1947 highway plan significantly predicts current road density, and (2) **Exclusion restriction**: The 1947 highway plan affects population growth only through its impact on road density, not through other channels.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s77_data.csv")

# Display basic summary statistics
cat("=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
summary(data)

# Check instrument relevance (First Stage)
cat("\n=== FIRST STAGE REGRESSION ===\n")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print(summary(first_stage))

# F-statistic for instrument strength
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:", f_stat, "\n")

if(f_stat > 10) {
  cat("Strong instrument (F > 10)\n")
} else {
  cat("Weak instrument concern (F < 10)\n")
}

# OLS estimation (biased baseline)
cat("\n=== OLS ESTIMATION (BIASED) ===\n")
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
print(summary(ols_model))

# IV estimation using 2SLS
cat("\n=== IV/2SLS ESTIMATION ===\n")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract and display key coefficient
iv_coeff <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
cat("\n=== MAIN RESULT ===\n")
cat("IV Coefficient of Road Density on Population Growth:", round(iv_coeff, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(iv_se, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(iv_coeff - 1.96*iv_se, 4), ",", round(iv_coeff + 1.96*iv_se, 4), "]\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Reduced form (effect of instrument on outcome)
cat("\n1. Reduced Form Regression:\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print(summary(reduced_form))

# 2. Compare OLS vs IV coefficients
cat("\n2. Coefficient Comparison:\n")
cat("OLS coefficient:", round(coef(ols_model)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("IV coefficient:", round(iv_coeff, 4), "\n")
cat("Difference:", round(iv_coeff - coef(ols_model)["x"], 4), "\n")

# 3. Test for endogeneity (Wu-Hausman test)
cat("\n3. Wu-Hausman Test for Endogeneity:\n")
# Manual implementation
resid_first <- residuals(first_stage)
endo_test <- lm(y ~ x + controls + resid_first, data = data)
endo_pvalue <- summary(endo_test)$coefficients["resid_first", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Wu-Hausman test p-value:", round(endo_pvalue, 4), "\n")
if(endo_pvalue < 0.05) {
  cat("Reject null: Evidence of endogeneity, IV preferred\n")
} else {
  cat("Fail to reject: No strong evidence of endogeneity\n")
}

# 4. Test instrument validity (if overidentified)
cat("\n4. Sample size and instrument coverage:\n")
cat("Total observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Observations with highway plan (z=1):", sum(data$z), "\n")
cat("Proportion with highway plan:", round(mean(data$z), 3), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **positive coefficient** of approximately **0.3 to 0.8**, indicating that higher road density causally increases urban population growth. The IV estimate should be larger than the OLS estimate, as road density endogeneity likely creates downward bias (areas anticipating slow growth may under-invest in roads). The 1947 highway plan provides plausibly exogenous variation since these infrastructure decisions were made based on mid-20th century priorities rather than contemporary growth expectations. The magnitude reflects that improved transportation infrastructure attracts residents and economic activity, but the effect is moderated by other urban development factors captured in controls.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use the 1947 highway plan as an instrument for road density.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased road density leads to higher population growth in urban areas.
